name: Overencumbered
oracle_text:
Enchant opponent
When this Aura enters, enchanted opponent creates a Clue token, a Food token, and a Junk token.
At the beginning of combat on enchanted opponent's turn, that player may pay {1} for each artifact they control. If they don't, creatures can't attack this combat.
blocked_sentences: When this Aura enters, enchanted opponent creates a Clue token, a Food token, and a Junk token.
At the beginning of combat on enchanted opponent's turn, that player may pay {1} for each artifact they control. If they don't, creatures can't attack this combat.

needs.what: an Aura whose host is a player rather than a permanent: GameObject.attached_to (and last_attached_to) able to hold a player id, stack._attach_aura attaching on a kind: 'player' target ref, and sba._aura_unattached treating a live player as a legal host
needs.why_existing_wont_do: A card-level target of kind 'player' with selector {'controller': 'opponent'} loads and targets correctly, but attached_to is typed int | None and means an oid; stack._attach_aura only attaches when ref.kind == 'object', so the Aura arrives attached to nothing and sba._aura_unattached immediately move_object()s it to the graveyard with cause 'aura_unattached'. Verified in the authoring sandbox: the only expectation that passes is zone 'graveyard' -- the card resolves, enchants nobody and dies before any of its abilities can matter

needs.what: a player spec (e.g. 'enchanted_player', beside 'controller_of' and 'owner_of' in effects.selectors.select_players) that names the player the source Aura is attached to, so an Aura's own triggered abilities can say 'enchanted opponent' and 'that player'
needs.why_existing_wont_do: PLAYER_SPEC_NAMES has only you/controller/each_opponent/opponent/each_player/all/active_player, none of which is 'the one this Aura is on'. {'target': 'enchanted'} is refused at compile -- loader line 1281 scopes an ability's target_kinds to that ability's own targets, so 'references target enchanted which the card does not declare'. Even if it loaded, ctx.target_players would return [] for a triggered ability and op_may reads nobody as ctx.controller, billing the Aura's own controller instead of the enchanted opponent -- the documented Rhystic Study failure. 'each_opponent' is the near miss and is wrong in multiplayer: it would tax every opponent, not the enchanted one

needs.what: a way to scope a phase trigger to one named player's turn -- either a trigger clause like {'active_player': 'enchanted_player'} or a condition key answering 'is it that player's turn', so 'at the beginning of combat on enchanted opponent's turn' fires exactly once, on the enchanted player's turn
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The begin_combat event exists, but TriggerModel.controller is only you/opponent/any: 'opponent' means any opponent's combat, which in multiplayer fires on every opponent's turn rather than the enchanted one's. condition_keys carries is_your_turn (the source's controller, the opposite player here) and cmp, but value_keys has no active-player term for a cmp to compare against

needs.what: an attack prohibition meaning 'creatures can't attack' full stop for a duration -- no legal defender at all, players, planeswalkers and battles alike
needs.why_existing_wont_do: cant_attack_player with attacker 'each_player' and defender 'each_player', duration 'this_combat', is the closest and installs the right cross-product (restrict_attack skips the self-pairs), but combat.attack_target_forbidden deliberately exempts planeswalkers -- 'attacking a planeswalker they control is not attacking the player', per its own docstring -- so creatures could still swing at a planeswalker under a line that prints 'creatures can't attack this combat'. The cant_attack static is the other near miss and cannot be limited to one combat: it is a continuous ability read off _battlefield_statics for as long as its source is on the battlefield, with no duration

closest_existing: may.pay with 'times' (the 'pay {1} for each artifact they control' half already works: {'mana':'{1}','times':{'count':{'zone':'battlefield','types':['Artifact'],'controller':'opponent'}}} compiles and is charged scaled)
